html:
SMTO-API-0009 — Your action doesn't fit the item's current state

GUID: 323f4d31-43bb-4fa1-a455-4dae20e796b1
Slug: api-state-conflict
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • The item you were working on has changed since this page last showed it. For example, it may already be running, finished, or edited in another tab, so SMTO turned the action down.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page to see the item's current state. The page may be showing an older view that offers an action that no longer applies.
  2. Check whether your earlier action already happened, for example whether the task is already running or your change is already saved. Another tab, device or person may have done it first, and repeating it could do it twice.
  3. Then use one of the buttons the reloaded page shows for that item. Those buttons match what the item can do right now.

What success looks like

  • The page shows the item's current state, and the action you choose completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the action from an old tab or page; reload it first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO endpoint returned HTTP 409 because the requested action conflicts with the resource's current state, and no more specific registered cause applied.

What this means

  • HTTP enrichment maps an otherwise unclassified status 409 to the state-conflict category without evidence of a specific revision change. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP enrichment maps an otherwise unclassified status 409 to the state-conflict category without evidence of a specific revision change.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the owning resource's current state and conflict detail before deciding whether a revision changed.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the resource from its owning endpoint, compare its current status or revision with the rejected request, and confirm whether the earlier action already took effect before submitting a new one; the response detail names the specific conflict.
  • Refresh the owning resource and resolve the specific state conflict before submitting a new action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate action meets the current resource's preconditions.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
